# Chapter 10 — From OrgPath to Policy Targeting — The Dynamic Group Library

::: {.callout-note}
## In this chapter
An attribute alone cannot be targeted by policy — only group memberships can. This chapter builds the dynamic group library that translates OrgPath values into policy-targetable groups: the node and branch group pair generated per OrgTree node, their membership rules, the creation pipeline, and the maintenance lifecycle as the OrgTree changes.
:::

## What the Dynamic Group Library Accomplishes

The dynamic group library is the set of Entra ID security groups — one pair per OrgTree node — that translates OrgPath attribute values into group memberships that policy surfaces can target. The OrgPath attribute, by itself, is a label on an identity object, and a label alone cannot be consumed by Intune, Conditional Access, Azure Policy, or Entitlement Management — those tools work with group memberships, not with arbitrary attribute values.

> The dynamic group library is the translation layer: **it creates the groups whose membership rules reference the OrgPath extension attribute,** ensuring that every identity in a given organizational position automatically becomes a member of the appropriate groups.

Any change to an identity's OrgPath value — triggered by the ETL pipeline — is automatically reflected in group membership within the Entra ID directory's asynchronous group processing window. Once the library is in place, policy targeting becomes a declaration of organizational position: an Intune device compliance policy targeted at the ORG-BRANCH-MKTDIG group applies to every device in the Digital Marketing team and every device in any sub-team beneath it, automatically, without any manual group management.

## Naming Convention and Group Design

Each node in the OrgTree generates exactly **two** Entra ID security groups — a node group and a branch group. They share the same node identifier but differ in scope: the node group matches a single level of the hierarchy, while the branch group matches that level and everything beneath it.

| Group | Name pattern | Membership rule | Selects |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Node group** | ORG-NODE-{nodeId} | (user.extension\_{appIdWithoutHyphens}\_OrgPath -eq "{nodePath}") | Every user and device whose OrgPath equals the node's path **exactly** |
| **Branch group** | ORG-BRANCH-{nodeId} | (user.extension\_{appIdWithoutHyphens}\_OrgPath -eq "{nodePath}") -or (user.extension\_{appIdWithoutHyphens}\_OrgPath -startsWith "{nodePath}/") | Every user and device at that node **or at any descendant node** |

For the node with id MKTDIG at path /COMM/MKT/MKTDIG, the two groups resolve as follows:

- The **node group** is named ORG-NODE-MKTDIG, with membership rule (user.extension\_{appIdWithoutHyphens}\_OrgPath -eq "/COMM/MKT/MKTDIG").
- The **branch group** is named ORG-BRANCH-MKTDIG, with membership rule (user.extension\_{appIdWithoutHyphens}\_OrgPath -eq "/COMM/MKT/MKTDIG") -or (user.extension\_{appIdWithoutHyphens}\_OrgPath -startsWith "/COMM/MKT/MKTDIG/").

The two groups serve different targeting intents:

- The **node group** is used for policies that should apply only to a specific level of the hierarchy — for example, a compliance policy specific to the Digital Marketing team but not to its sub-teams.
- The **branch group** is used for policies that should apply to an entire subtree — for example, an Intune configuration profile that applies to everyone in Commercial and all of its descendant units, targeted at ORG-BRANCH-COMM.

## The Group Creation Pipeline

The dynamic group library is created by the pipeline script New-OrgGroupLibrary.ps1, which reads the OrgTree registry from the governance repository, enumerates all nodes with Active or Pending status, and for each node makes two POST requests to the Microsoft Graph API endpoint /v1.0/groups.

Each POST request body specifies the following properties:

| Property | Value | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **displayName** | The group's display name | Human-readable label (ORG-NODE-{nodeId} or ORG-BRANCH-{nodeId}) |
| **mailNickname** | A URL-safe version of the display name | Required by the API even for non-mail-enabled groups |
| **groupTypes** | Array containing the single value DynamicMembership | Marks the group as dynamic |
| **securityEnabled** | true | Makes the group a security group |
| **mailEnabled** | false | The group is not mail-enabled |
| **membershipRule** | The node or branch rule string | Defines membership against the OrgPath extension attribute |
| **membershipRuleProcessingState** | On (or Paused) | Activates the rule on creation; see below |

The membershipRuleProcessingState property should be set to On to activate the rule immediately upon group creation. A value of Paused creates the group with an inactive rule, which is useful for staged deployment scenarios where the engineering team wants to validate the group definition before membership processing begins.

After each group is created, the pipeline records the group's id (the Entra object ID returned in the creation response) against the corresponding OrgTree node id in a group registry file at registry/group-registry.yaml.

> This file is **the authoritative mapping** between OrgTree node ids and Entra group object IDs, and is committed to the governance repository after every group creation or modification operation.

## Group Library Maintenance Lifecycle

The group library is a living construct that changes as the OrgTree changes. When a structural change is merged to main, the post-receive webhook fires the propagation pipeline, which reconciles the live group library against the new OrgTree. How it responds depends on the kind of change:

| OrgTree change | Propagation pipeline action |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Node added** | Reads the new OrgTree, identifies nodes with no entry in the group registry, creates the node and branch groups for those new nodes using the same POST sequence described above, and updates the group registry with the new group IDs |
| **Node renamed** (name field changes, id field does not) | Updates the displayName of both associated groups via a PATCH to /v1.0/groups/{groupObjectId} with a JSON body containing only the updated displayName |
| **Node deprecated** | Updates the description field of both groups to include a deprecation notice with the effective date, but does **not** delete the groups |
| **Node archived** | Confirms neither group is referenced in any active policy, then proceeds with deletion (see below) |

A few points warrant emphasis. On a **rename**, the membershipRule does not change, because it is based on the node's id and path, neither of which changes when the display name changes.

On a **deprecation**, the groups are retained because active policy assignments may reference them during the transition period, and deleting them would immediately remove those policy targets.

On an **archive**, the propagation pipeline first queries the Graph API to confirm that neither group is referenced in any current Conditional Access policy, Intune assignment, or Entitlement Management access package — using the /v1.0/groups/{groupId}/transitiveMemberOf endpoint and the policy assignment endpoints — and only proceeds with deletion after confirming no active references exist.
